sourceLabel: Audited consolidated financial results filed with the exchanges
coverage: Whole-group totals · one reported business segment (pharmaceutical and related products)
definition: Profit for the year after all expenses, exceptional items, tax and the share of associates’ result. It includes a small loss that belongs to minority owners of subsidiaries and is not operating profit or cash flow.
location: Audited consolidated financial results for the year ended 31 March 2026, filed 13 May 2026: PDF page 3 (printed page 1/5), year ended 31-03-2026 column; notes 4, 9 and 10 on PDF pages 6–7
notes: Revenue is total revenue from operations (sale of products ₹27,711.69 crore plus other operating revenue ₹450.90 crore) and excludes other income of ₹882.01 crore. Net profit for the year is ₹3,861.74 crore, of which ₹3,879.23 crore belongs to owners of Cipla and −₹17.49 crore to non-controlling interests. It is after an exceptional expense of ₹275.91 crore for the new Labour Codes (higher gratuity and leave liabilities from the changed definition of wages), a ₹42.02 crore write-down of investments in associates, and a tax charge of ₹1,353.84 crore that includes a deferred-tax credit of ₹87.11 crore. Cipla reports a single operating segment, so profit by product or market is not disclosed.
insight: Cipla kept about 14 paise of profit from each rupee of revenue after a one-time labour-law cost and a tax charge. These totals cannot show how much comes from India, the US or other markets.
